anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet (mcu.kicad_sch), U10 (TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) pin 1 IN is connected to NET0010, but pin 2 DIAG_EN has no wire, label, or no-connect marker. The drawing shows NET0010 only tied to U10 pin 1 and to U7 GPIO1/ADC1_CH1/XTAL_32K_N (pin 13).
anomalies.expected: The specification states that the heater switch is driven from ESP32 GPIO1 on both IN and DIAG_EN: "IN/DIAG_EN (pins 1/2) are both driven from ESP32 GPIO1 (net /Microcontroller/HEATER)." Pin 2 should therefore be connected to the same GPIO1/HEATER net as pin 1.

evidence.quote: MCU sheet, mcu.kicad_sch: U10 TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1, pin 1 IN wired to NET0010; pin 2 DIAG_EN has no wire/label, while pin 5 DELAY is explicitly marked with an X.
driven by ESP32 GPIO1 on both IN and DIAG_EN

anomalies.impact: The TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1 DIAG_EN pin is left floating rather than being driven with the heater control signal. This can leave the device's diagnostic/enable state undefined or different from the intended design, potentially affecting reliable heater switching or fault behavior.

parsed.summary: The schematic otherwise follows the described CF-Chef architecture, but the heater smart high-side switch appears to have its DIAG_EN pin unconnected even though the specification requires it to be driven from the same GPIO1/HEATER net as IN.
